blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Mask the keys too (`safe[maskEmails(key)] = …`), so that a caller logging a map keyed by address — `logInfo("retries", { "ada.lovelace@example.org": 3 })` — does not write `{"ada.lovelace@example.org":3}` in full to the logs the hosting provider keeps 90 days (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), 25). The proposal promises masking of "every e-mail address in the message and the fields"; add a `logInfo` test covering a key and a value.
findings.title: Field keys are written to the log unmasked

findings.recommendation: The character classes are ASCII-only and the local part must run unbroken up to the `@`, so `josé@example.org` or `ada@exämple.org` (valid internationalised addresses, RFC 6531) match nothing and are logged in full — the proposal's "every e-mail address" is not met. Match the local part and domain on any non-space, non-`@` characters (e.g. `/([^\s@])[^\s@]*@([^\s@]+\.[^\s@]{2,})/gu`) and add a test with an accented address.
findings.title: Addresses with non-ASCII characters escape the mask entirely

findings.recommendation: A logged URL such as `/reset?email=ada%40example.org` carries the address without a literal `@`, so it passes through unmasked. Whether callers log such URLs could not be verified; if they do, also match `%40` as the separator.
findings.title: Percent-encoded addresses in logged URLs are not masked

findings.recommendation: For a personal or small custom domain (`a***@lovelace.family`) the kept initial and domain can re-identify the customer. Confirm with the team that the domain is needed for the logs' purpose; otherwise mask it as well, or replace the address with a keyed hash (data minimisation, GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)).
findings.title: The mask keeps the first letter and the full domain
